rationale: B wins because it separates the outside-validation story from the regulatory story: "A sleep clinic agreed to study a consumer mattress. Here is what it is measuring." gives a reporter a real institutional protagonist. A's "Eight Sleep's new mattress sensors track blood oxygen and snoring, but the company won't call it diagnostic" is solid, but it makes the clinic do side duty instead of assigning it its own story. The difference is proof discipline: B asks for PI, endpoints, sample size, funding, and registration; A spends one slot on "For athletes chasing recovery data," which is a soft audience premise wearing a press badge.
gaps_in_A: "a live clinical study with an unnamed sleep clinic" contradicts the update's "named sleep clinic" fact and turns one of the few hard verification assets into self-created fog.
"For athletes chasing recovery data" stretches "markets to athletes and biohackers" into a recovery-use story without evidence or a named user.

"Beds are becoming health sensors" is a one-company trend unless Eight Sleep can supply comparable examples; A admits it needs "other examples of ambient/passive health sensing" before the category claim holds.
It buries the clinic inside the regulatory angle instead of building a separate clinic-as-protagonist angle around study design, endpoints, funding, and what the results could actually prove.
gaps_in_B: "This bed changes its temperature while you are doing it" overstates timing and causality; the update does not prove the bed reacts during a snore or oxygen drop.
"appears on a customer's phone" invents the user surface. The update gives the mattress cover and subscription tier, not the app or display experience.
"defensive-comment" is the wrong label; no controversy or inbound criticism exists in the supplied facts, so this is regulatory accountability, not a defensive posture.
"Eight Sleep is privately held" is dumped into the subscription angle without becoming a story point. If ownership is not tied to disclosure, pricing pressure, or investor strategy, cut it.
